module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1072

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1072](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1072)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Filter Finset Set
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos1072

/-- For any prime $p$, let $f(p)$ be the least integer such that $f(p)! + 1 \equiv 0 \mod p$. -/
noncomputable def f (p : ℕ) : ℕ := sInf {n | (n)! + 1 ≡ 0 [MOD p]}

/-- Is it true that there are infinitely many $p$ for which $f(p) = p − 1$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} := by
  sorry

/-- Is it true that $f(p)/p \to 0$ for $p \to \infty$ in a density 1 subset of the primes? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (P : Set ℕ), P ⊆ {p | p.Prime} ∧ P.HasDensity 1 {p | p.Prime} ∧
      Tendsto (fun p => (f p / p : ℝ)) (atTop ⊓ principal P) (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry
/--
Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao [HaSu02], believed that the number of $p \le x$ for which $f(p)=p−1$
is $o(x/\log x)$.

[HaSu02] Hardy, G. E. and Subbarao, M. V., _A modified problem of Pillai and some related questions._
Amer. Math. Monthly (2002), 554--559.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.variants.littleo :
    (fun x ↦ (({p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} ∩ Icc 0 x).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x ↦ x / Real.log x) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1072

reformulations.difference: `f p := sInf {n | n ! + 1 ≡ 0 [MOD p]}` takes the minimum over all of ℕ, 0 included. So `f 2 = 0` (0! + 1 = 2 ≡ 0 mod 2). If the source's "least integer" means least positive integer, f(2) = 1 = 2 − 1. Then 2 lies in the source's set {p : f(p) = p − 1} but not in the Lean set `{p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1}`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Wilson gives (p−1)! ≡ −1 (mod p), so for every prime the set is nonempty and `f p ≤ p − 1`; `sInf ∅` is never reached. For an odd prime, 0! + 1 = 1! + 1 = 2 ≢ 0 (mod p), so `f p ≥ 2` and agrees with the least-positive reading f'. Only p = 2 differs. One prime changes neither the infinitude in parts.i, nor a limit along `atTop ⊓ 𝓟 P` in parts.ii (the two functions agree for p ≥ 3), nor an o(x/log x) count, since the counts differ by exactly 1 for x ≥ 2 and 1 = o(x/log x). In a scratch file I defined `f' p := sInf {n | 0 < n ∧ n ! + 1 ≡ 0 [MOD p]}` and proved: `f p = f' p` for primes p ≠ 2; `f' 2 = 1`; `f 2 = 0`. I also proved all three `↔`s with zero errors: `Set.Infinite {p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} ↔ Set.Infinite {p | p.Prime ∧ f' p = p - 1}`, the parts.ii right-hand side for f ↔ for f', and the littleo statement for f ↔ for f'.

reformulations.difference: The source's "f(p)/p → 0 for almost all p" is rendered as: there is P ⊆ primes with relative natural density 1 in the primes (`P.HasDensity 1 {p | p.Prime}`) such that `Tendsto (fun p => (f p / p : ℝ)) (atTop ⊓ 𝓟 P) (𝓝 0)`. It is not phrased as "for every ε > 0, the primes with f(p) ≥ εp have relative density 0".
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two readings are equivalent by the standard diagonal argument. (⇒) Along P, eventually f(p)/p < ε, so E_ε = {p prime : f(p) ≥ εp} ⊆ (primes \ P) ∪ (a finite set). Both have relative density 0: P has density 1 and P ⊆ primes, and a finite set has density 0 because π(b) → ∞. (⇐) E_{1/k} increases with k. Choose b_1 < b_2 < … with #(E_{1/k} ∩ [0,b)) ≤ π(b)/k for b ≥ b_k, and set P = primes \ ⋃_k (E_{1/k} ∩ [b_k, ∞)). Then f(p)/p < 1/k for p ∈ P with p ≥ b_k. For b ∈ [b_k, b_{k+1}), the excluded part below b lies in E_{1/k}, so it has relative size ≤ 1/k, and P has relative density 1. A finite or density-0 P cannot satisfy `HasDensity P 1`, so the filter `atTop ⊓ 𝓟 P` is non-trivial and the condition is not vacuous. Lower density 1 and density 1 coincide, so using `HasDensity` loses nothing.

review.notes:
No misformalizations found. All three statements match the cited source (erdosproblems.com/1072, read through a verbatim scrape because the live site was behind Cloudflare during this review):
- parts.i: `answer(sorry) ↔ {p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1}.Infinite` is \"infinitely many p with f(p) = p − 1\".
- parts.ii: \"f(p)/p → 0 for almost all p\" is rendered as convergence along a subset of the primes with relative density 1. I checked the elaborated term: the division is real (`↑(f p) / ↑p`), the density is relative to `{p | p.Prime}`, and the filter is `atTop ⊓ 𝓟 P`.
- variants.littleo: #{p ≤ x prime : f(p) = p − 1} = o(x / log x) over x : ℕ. This is equivalent to the real-variable version, because the count is constant between integers and ⌊x⌋/log⌊x⌋ ~ x/log x.
- The docstrings match the source. None of the statements is vacuous. Junk values (sInf ∅ = 0, log 0 = log 1 = 0, truncated p − 1) are unreachable or irrelevant under atTop.

Numerics (a Perl check, not part of the file): about 36–39% of primes up to 30000 have f(p) = p − 1, close to 1/e. So the questions are not trivially settled; the data lean against part (ii) and the EHS belief, but nothing is proved.

Status: all three are tagged `research open`, consistent with the source and the teorth database (open). No status issues.

Limitations: I could not read the live erdosproblems.com page, the Hardy–Subbarao paper (closed access), or Guy's A2 (restricted). The o(x/log x) belief was therefore checked against the erdosproblems.com wording only. Since o(x/log x) = o(π(x)), any usual phrasing of it is equivalent.
